cars.variant: Fury V-800 318 two-door hardtop — 1957 USA factory folder, three-speed manual
cars.specification_market: 1957 USA Fury two-door hardtop with 318 V-800 and standard three-speed synchromesh manual, using the dedicated Plymouth Fury showroom folder as the factory reference. Count the original 1956–1958 Fury performance-road programme once across years, engines and associated Belvedere identities. No later full-size Fury, Super Stock, Christine replica or race specifications. Dimensions and equipment are brochure values, not the slightly different road-test measurements. No road-test acceleration, altered ignition/linkage, shipping mass as curb weight, sales total, modern net conversion or universal axle-ratio claim.
cars.summary: The original Fury is an important early American performance-road programme, pairing a dual-carb V8 with a deliberately uprated torsion-bar chassis. Racer Brown’s contemporary 1957 first-hand test establishes exceptional period handling significance while documenting braking limitations, supporting admission beyond styling, rarity or later film fame.

sources.title: 1957 Fury by Plymouth — showroom folder, engineering descriptions
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer showroom/specification brochure, hosted scan
sources.notes: Four-page scanned PDF, 5,391,010 bytes. Full PDF indexes 1 and 3 visually read; engineering region on 3 enlarged and read. Other pages not individually audited. Selected factory specification: 318 V-800, 290 advertised hp, three-speed manual. Keep showroom dimensions 206.0/79.4/53.5 inches separate from period road-test figures. Factory folder lists 3.54 manual axle while other compilations differ; no axle ratio imported. Tyres are blackwall standard, whitewall optional in this folder. The 3,625-lb figure is estimated shipping weight, not imported curb mass.

sources.title: Plymouth: Fury vs. Stock — Racer Brown, May 1957
sources.source_type: Contemporary first-hand road test, publisher archive
sources.notes: Original May 1957 test republished January 2023. Admission evidence: more than 1,500 miles of Fury testing, praise for chassis balance and a documented brake-fade criticism. Test car had a three-speed manual. Test-specific ignition changes, carburettor linkage experiments and acceleration are not imported factory performance claims.
